name: Tax — consumables the contractor owes, rentals the owner owes
$source: The rule the PM applies by hand on every application and the review never did: on this contract the tax on things bought and consumed or kept is the contractor's, and the tax on equipment rented for the job is a reimbursable cost. Charges below are the shapes these actually arrive in — a rental house invoice, a furniture purchase inside a subcontractor breakdown, fuel, and one line too terse to place.

contract.taxExemptBasis: Owner is a Texas independent school district

categories.basis: Rental charges for construction equipment, including taxes thereon, shall be a Cost of the Work
Taxes on supplies consumed in the performance of the Work shall be borne by the Contractor
Taxes on equipment and furnishings purchased and retained by the Contractor or its Subcontractors are not reimbursable

taxes.description: Site office furniture - desks and chairs
Cut-off blades, gloves and safety supplies

findings.why: $412.50 of tax on office furniture, which this contract makes the contractor absorb
$66.00 of tax on diesel fuel — a consumable, the contractor's own cost
$18.15 of tax on blades and safety supplies, rolled up as one note under the $25 floor
$339.84 of tax on a tax-exempt job that says only "Tax" — including the $21.44 the retired S7 used to catch, now raised at the same weight but without pretending to know what was bought
